intent: Three low countries, one that is barely there: the high points side by side, the wall around the capital against the metre-and-a-half average, then the underwater cabinet meeting that made the world look.
pacing_profile: question read verbatim, three options, 3-s beat, reveal with the number, story beats shaped per episode (brief.md), punchline + short follow
pause_policy: Pause only at the marked ellipses; the beat is real silence (ticks come from quizscore.py).
title: Which is the FLATTEST country on Earth?

lines.direction: the question, cold — curiosity comes from the map moving under it
lines.text: Which is the flattest country on Earth?

lines.direction: quick, each option its own beat

lines.text: The Maldives. Its highest natural point is about 5 metres; most of its 1,190 islands sit far lower.

lines.direction: ease back so the atoll chain fills the frame; the three high-point columns rise on 'Netherlands' with the Maldives bar barely visible; a mountain sticker; the Dutch flag-ball thinks on 'Denmark'; a palm sticker on 'tree' as the Maldives pulses
lines.text: The Netherlands reaches 322 metres. Denmark tops out at 171. The Maldives cannot clear a tree.

lines.direction: tighten on Malé; the 1.5 M / 3 M split lands on 'average'; the Malé pin on 'capital'; a brick-wall sticker and the sea-wall tag on 'wall'; the Maldives pulses
lines.text: Average ground level is a metre and a half. The capital, Malé, hides behind a sea wall 3 metres high.

lines.direction: ease back over the central atolls; a diver sticker and the 2009 card on 'cabinet'; a pen on 'signing'; the Maldivian flag-ball grins and the islands pulse on 'watched'; the Malé pin leaves at the end
lines.text: In 2009 the cabinet met underwater in scuba gear, signing a plea on rising seas. The world watched.

lines.direction: punchline, then a short follow — the outro visual asks
lines.text: Lower than a house. Follow us.
